title: Primary Care Referrals and Prior Authorization Transition-of-Care Units
content:
**Rule.** The referral addition of a transition-of-care request looks at the referrals the member's primary care provider issued in the two months before the day the request is recorded: where a standing referral was issued, two units are added; where only a single referral was issued, one unit is added; where no referral was issued, nothing is added.

The referrals are the referral issue entries on the member's Primary Care Provider Assignment, each marked as a standing or a single referral. The addition is made once to the units a Prior Authorization transition-of-care request asks for, before the ceiling of the class's most units per approval is applied.

## Training questions

**Q: The primary care provider issued one standing and one single referral in the two months. What is added?**
A: 2 units. Where a standing referral was issued, the addition is two units.

**Q: Two single referrals and no standing referral were issued. What is added?**
A: 1 unit. The addition for single referrals does not grow with their number.

**Q: The only referral was issued before the two-month window. What is added?**
A: Nothing, because no referral was issued in the two months before the request day.

| Referrals issued in the two months before the request day | Units added |
|---|---|
| at least one standing referral | 2 |
| single referrals only | 1 |
| none | 0 |
